To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structural relaxation and the (Non-JC) β-relaxation processes are correlated in Poly(viny1 acetate) over wide temperature range.
the dynamics of α- and JG β-processes are correlated at PVAc over a wide temperature and pressure range.
the structural relaxation time of Poly(vinylacetate) is not correlated with the relaxation time of the (Non-JOG) β-processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the glass from systems that are strongly correlated in the primary α- relaxation and the (Non-Jg) β-relaxation processes.
the study of the dynamics in the glassy state of Poly(vinylacetate) (PVAc).
the study of the dielectric relaxation of a glass from the systems that the dynamics is strongly correlated in PVAc.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (Non-Jg) β-processes doesnot act as a precursor of structural relaxation.
the JG-β-processes are the precursor of the structural α-relaxation, but the (Non-J-G) β-relaxation is not.
the (Non-Jg) β-processes is not a precursor of the α-relaxation in PVAc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (J.G.) β-processes relaxation is not a precursor for the structural relaxation at PVAC.
the structural relaxation is not directly related with the β-relaxation processes.
the (Jg) β-process is not a universal process but it depends on the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric relaxation of a glassy polymer at different isobaric- isothermal paths is a very complex phenomenon.
the dielectric relaxation of PVAc can be understood as the result of a complex interaction between the primary α- process and the secondary β-processes.
the dielectric relaxation of the α-process in PVAc is not affected by the pressure.
